title: The AI provider resolver probes EVERY CLI, below the winner too, with no single-flight, on the request path
what: In AUTO, resolved() probes every CLI provider whose 600 s cache entry expired (two subprocesses each: --version and a real one-token call), although resolve_provider takes the first available and the lower probes can only change the reason string. probe_cli holds no lock across the spawn, so concurrent callers at expiry each spawn their own pair.
cost: Every 600 s of AI use the first Cards/ytdl/Settings call pays Claude Code's probe plus Codex's probe serially before its real call: measured 4 spawns per resolve (2 wasted), 32 spawns for 8 concurrent resolves. Estimated ~200 MB RSS per spawn of the 238 MB CLI, 5-20 s added latency warm and up to minutes cold, ~50 billed probe calls per CLI per working day, doubled with Codex installed.
evidence: probe_herd.py with stubbed _run: single resolve -> claude_code chosen, spawns claude_code --version 1, -p 1, codex --version 1, exec 1; 8 concurrent -> 32 spawns. No early exit in the PROVIDER_ORDER loop; _probe_lock guards only the dict.
ledger: new; related to ytdl-web-5 (pinned case only) and CR-121
fix: In AUTO probe in chain order and stop at the first available (rows below from unprobed_cli_state); per-provider lock in probe_cli so concurrent callers share one in-flight probe; optionally refresh the cache on a successful real call. Keep force=True, the pin refusal, CR-121 and CR-355 behaviour.

title: Every OTA apply copies every database twice, including a ~500 MB b-roll index it almost never migrates, and keeps up to eight such copies
what: apply copies dashboard.db, broll.db and music.db into staging/.dbcheck for stage-verify, then copies all three again into /data/backups/<ts>-before-<v>/ whether or not the new code migrates them. Per-version labels mean retention is 8 backups or 8 GiB.
cost: Per apply ~1 GB written for b-roll alone (2 x ~500 MB), estimated 10-20 s extra I/O on a NAS HDD pool; steady state ~4.2 GB of /data held (8 x ~520 MB) on the volume dashboard.db lives on; preflight's 2x-db free-space demand refuses updates earlier than needed at larger sites.
evidence: Code read (no branch skips an unmigrated DB); E: roll-queue roll.db = 501,460,992 bytes; music.db = 20,537,344 bytes.
fix: Have stage-verify report each DB's user_version before/after migrating its copy, and back up only the DBs whose version moved (always dashboard.db). Keep REL-10's backup_for_version, restore_backup and the preflight.

title: Interrupted downloads on the two UNATTENDED paths leave staging files that nothing sweeps
what: A kill during fetch_artifact_to leaves packages/<platform>/<file>.<uuid>.part (up to 200 MiB); the only sweeper runs inside the human PUT route, which a feed-only customer never calls. A kill mid-apply leaves code/<v>.tar.gz.part (never swept) and code/<v>.staging/ with ~520 MB of .dbcheck copies, removed only by a later apply's prune_code_trees; the healed state is 'failed' and auto-apply never retries a failed version.
cost: 0.2-0.8 GB of /data per interrupted fetch or apply, held indefinitely; rare but cumulative on the shell-less appliance.
evidence: Code read; _sweep_stale_parts has one call site (api.py:7703).
ledger: new; same shape as REL-15 (fixed for the CLI .staging)
fix: Sweep stale .part in publish_from_feed before downloading; in _heal_orphaned_progress, where the dead latch is cleared, remove code/*.tar.gz.part and code/*.staging.

title: The sign-in pty master fd is closed from two threads without the session lock, and while the reader thread may still read it
what: _kill reads and clears session._master without a lock; CANCEL runs it on the request thread while the worker loop runs it too, so both can close the same fd number, the second closing whatever reused it. The worker also closes the master after reader.join(timeout=2) while the reader may still loop on os.read(master). No wait() after proc.kill().
cost: Needs a CANCEL or timeout racing the child's exit, or a grandchild holding the slave; result is one stolen/closed descriptor in the dashboard process (an HTTP request or DB handle failing once). A few sign-ins per site per year.
fix: Swap the fd under session._lock and let only the reader close it on EOF/EIO; add proc.wait(timeout) after proc.kill().

title: The release runbook restarts the dashboard to force a feed check that a button already does, and soaking/staged records wait a whole poll interval
what: Pathway B step 5 says to docker restart the dashboard to trigger a feed check now; Check now (POST /api/v1/admin/feed/check) does the same without stopping Cards engines, the /cards/edit child and running ytdl jobs. The soak gates are re-evaluated only inside check_now, which runs daily.
cost: One avoidable container restart per studio release (estimated 10-60 s down plus lost in-flight work); on policy=current customer sites up to 24 h between a 30-minute soak ending and the build being offered (latency part PLAUSIBLE, depends on site policy).
fix: Point the runbook at Check now (or have publish_latest.py call the check route); re-run _apply_policy/apply_dashboard_policy hourly against the cached verified channel with no fetch and no re-verify.
